problem: The stated ranges (8-15 mm offset from the cavity surface, 6-12 mm channel diameter) are much larger than the usual conformal-cooling practice for small and medium inserts; a student will size channels wrongly for a phone-cover type mould. Typical practice is a channel about 1.5 to 2 channel diameters away from the surface, with diameters of roughly 3-8 mm; the big values only apply to very large moulds.
fix: Say: 'commonly 3 to 8 mm diameter, placed about 1.5 to 2 channel diameters (roughly 5 to 12 mm) from the cavity surface; large moulds use bigger channels.'

where: Section 2, first paragraph of the cooling description
problem: 'with round bends instead of drilled plugs' is unclear — a drilled circuit needs cross-drilled holes closed with plugs, and the student may think the plug is a feature of the channel shape.
fix: Say: 'with smooth bends, instead of the cross-drilled holes with plugged ends that a drilled cooling circuit needs.'

problem: c_part is described as 'the cost of one part on the machine', but for a tooling route the part is made on the moulding press, not on the AM machine, so 'the machine' is ambiguous.
fix: Define it as: 'c_part is the cost of making one part by the production route being compared (material, machine hour rate of that machine × cycle time, labour) in ₹.'

problem: Cycle time is the time per moulding shot, not per part. Treating 10 s saved as 10 s saved per part is only true for a single-cavity mould, and the example does not say so.
fix: Add one line: 'Assume a single-cavity mould, so one shot makes one part and the cycle-time saving equals the saving per part.'
